title: Spanakopita
subtitle: Greek spinach and feta pie in filo pastry
excerpt: The great Greek savoury pastry: layers of buttered filo encasing a filling of spinach, feta, dill, and eggs, baked until the pastry is shatteringly crisp and the filling is set and fragrant. Eaten warm or at room temperature.

recipe.sourceNotes: Spanakopita (spanaki means spinach, pita means pie) is one of the defining preparations of Greek cuisine, made in homes and bakeries across Greece and eaten as a mezze, snack, or main course. The dish exists in regional variations across the Balkans and the eastern Mediterranean, reflecting the shared culinary heritage of the Ottoman period. In Greece it is made as a large tray pie (koulouri), individual triangles (trigona), or rolled (strifta). The filling always contains spinach and feta; the additions of dill, spring onion, eggs, and ricotta (to stretch the feta) vary by family. Filo pastry must be kept covered with a damp cloth while working to prevent it drying out and cracking; each sheet must be brushed with butter or olive oil to keep the layers separate during baking.

content.text: Squeeze the spinach as dry as possible: wet spinach makes the pastry soggy. Keep unused filo under a damp tea towel while working. Brush each filo sheet with melted butter all the way to the edges; unbuttered patches will remain dry and tough. Score the top layers of pastry before baking so the steam can escape and the pie does not puff and crack.

items.preparation: fresh; or 400 g frozen spinach, thawed

content.text: Wilt the fresh spinach in a hot pan with a splash of water, then drain and squeeze in a clean cloth until very dry. If using frozen, thaw and squeeze dry. Roughly chop. Mix the spinach with the crumbled feta, beaten eggs, spring onion, dill, nutmeg, and pepper. Taste: it should be well seasoned. The feta provides most of the salt so add only a little if needed.

Heat the oven to 190 C (170 C fan). Brush a 30 x 20 cm baking tin with butter. Layer 6 sheets of filo in the tin, brushing each sheet generously with melted butter and letting the edges overhang. Spread the filling evenly over the filo. Fold the overhanging filo over the filling. Layer the remaining 6 sheets on top, brushing each with butter. Tuck the edges down inside the tin.

Score the top layers of pastry into portions with a sharp knife. Bake for 40 to 45 minutes until the top is deeply golden and crisp. Cool in the tin for 10 minutes before cutting along the scored lines. Serve warm or at room temperature.
